definitions.explanation: costs that change in proportion to the volume of production or business activity, as opposed to fixed costs

examples.japanese: {材料費|ざいりょうひ}は{変動費|へんどうひ}に{分類|ぶんるい}される。
examples.english: Material costs are classified as variable costs.

examples.japanese: {売上|うりあげ}が{増|ふ}えると{変動費|へんどうひ}も{増加|ぞうか}する。
examples.english: When sales increase, variable costs also increase.

examples.japanese: {変動費|へんどうひ}と{固定費|こていひ}の{割合|わりあい}を{把握|はあく}することで、{損益分岐点|そんえきぶんきてん}を{計算|けいさん}できる。
examples.english: By understanding the ratio of variable costs to fixed costs, you can calculate the break-even point.

notes:
Composed of {変動|へんどう} (fluctuation; change) + {費|ひ} (cost; expense). A fundamental accounting and business term. Typical examples of variable costs include {原材料費|げんざいりょうひ} (raw material costs), {送料|そうりょう} (shipping costs), and {販売手数料|はんばいてすうりょう} (sales commissions).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {変動費|へんどうひ}を{削減|さくげん}する: to reduce variable costs
- {変動費|へんどうひ}{率|りつ}: variable cost ratio
- {変動費|へんどうひ}と{固定費|こていひ}: variable costs and fixed costs
- {変動費|へんどうひ}の{内訳|うちわけ}: breakdown of variable costs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {固定費|こていひ}: fixed costs — costs that remain constant regardless of production volume (e.g., rent, salaries)
- {経費|けいひ}: expenses — a broader term covering all business costs
- {原価|げんか}: cost price — the direct cost of producing a product
